newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras eyes $200 mln samurai bond.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras eyes $200 mln samurai bond.

text.p: Brazil's federally owned oil firm Petrobras plans to issue $200 million in debt denominated in Japanese yen by June, said Hernani Fortuna, the company's chief of financial planning division.
"We are likely to tap the Japanese market by issuing about $200 million worth of samurai bonds by June," Fortuna said. He did not mention a maturity period for the bonds.
Fortuna, speaking at a conference on Latin American utilities sponsored by Caspian Securities, said the issue still needs approval from the Central Bank and the Senate.
"We are discussing with the government if the samurai bond issue is the best alternative," Fortuna said, adding that the Central Bank could recommend issuing bonds in another currency.
Other likely alternatives would be Deutsche marks or U.S. dollars, he said.
Petrobras was meeting with Japanese credit rating agencies to rate the deal.

The samurai bonds would be the first of a total of between $500 million and $600 million in debt the company plans to issue in 1997. Last year, Petrobras raised $500 million from the Eurobond market, Fortuna said.

The money would be raised to finance new investment, he said, adding the company did not have to roll over a large amount of debt this year. Petrobras has said it plans to invest $3.0 billion a year between 1996 and 2000.
Fortuna also said the company was preparing to list its stock on U.S. stock exchanges.

"We are beginning now to work on adjusting our accounting practices to U.S. standards so we can list our stock on an American exchange," he said, adding the New York Stock Exchange has shown a strong interest in having Petrobras list its shares.
